title: Career Roadmap · Weaver
summary: A Weaver operates handlooms or power looms to produce fabric, textiles and traditional woven products, using knowledge of yarn, patterns, loom operation, fabric quality and production techniques.

blocks.label: Recommended
blocks.text: Complete Class 10 for eligible vocational routes; Class 12 can expand further-study options.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: No specific stream is universally required for vocational weaving training.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Textile fibres, yarn types, fabric structures, weaving patterns, colour combinations and textile design.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Hand coordination, pattern recognition, precision, creativity and basic mathematics.

rows.text: Garment construction and understanding fabric use
Yarn, fabric manufacturing, processing and quality
Textile patterns, woven structures and design development

blocks.text: DGT lists Weaving Technician as a one-year CTS trade with Class 10 entry, and Weaving Technician for Silk & Woollen Fabrics as a one-year trade with Class 8 entry. The curriculum and course availability may vary; confirm with the current official listing.

blocks.label: Year 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Yarn types, loom components, warp and weft, basic weave structures and fabric inspection.

blocks.label: Year 2 — Technical skills
blocks.text: Loom setup, weaving patterns, tension control, defect identification and production efficiency.

blocks.label: Year 3 — Advanced skills
blocks.text: Complex patterns, design development, colour combinations, computer-aided textile design and industry experience.

blocks.label: Year 4 — Career preparation
blocks.text: Specialize in handloom or industrial weaving, document sample fabrics and prepare for jobs or further study.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Plain-weave and twill sample book • Traditional motif collection • Fabric defect inspection sheet • Costing and production-time comparison.
